### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 08bf7d2a41a754c601af90281446acf38c3169ec` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6f38ede00f36b2f837085843a4515610432571ce` — the merge of head `344fc148d28a5cbbb1ad4ba7cddcdca97d372a17` into base `08bf7d2a41a754c601af90281446acf38c3169ec`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6f38ede00f36b2f837085843a4515610432571ce && git checkout 6f38ede00f36b2f837085843a4515610432571ce
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 08bf7d2a41a754c601af90281446acf38c3169ec 344fc148d28a5cbbb1ad4ba7cddcdca97d372a17 && git checkout -B drift-repro 08bf7d2a41a754c601af90281446acf38c3169ec && git merge --no-ff 344fc148d28a5cbbb1ad4ba7cddcdca97d372a17

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 08bf7d2a41a754c601af90281446acf38c3169ec
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 08bf7d2a41a754c601af90281446acf38c3169ec` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `db0a77a90995c5c6487a521978f1cd05d86b3062`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-bare-save-dependent-only-member-35524.test.ts + .changeset/35524-bare-save-follows-base-dependent-member.md (read for ② only, not ④-reviewed)
Security-touching: no
Rule-change-verified: none

Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset, `!` in the title). PR #37069, card #35524. Read: the net diff against `main`, the card and its four comments, the check-runs on the head, and, outside the diff, the code the hunks cite (`rowHeldBaseAddressOf` and `rowHeldBaseJudgment` in `protocol-meta-item-face.ts`, `packagelessDraftAddress` and `strictDraftReadAddress` in `protocol-lock-version-gates.ts`, `packagelessAddress` in `protocol-environment-rows.ts`, the delete door in `protocol-diff-delete-load.ts`, the per-item publish in `protocol-history-and-publish.ts`, `historySlotOf` in `protocol-history-slots.ts`, `packagelessHolderRefusal` and the writable-package gate in `protocol-save.ts`). Nothing built or run. Check-runs on the head: every completed run is `success` or `skipped` (Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Test Core 1..10, TypeScript Type Check, Lint & Repo Gates, Dogfood Regression Gate, Governed Surface Queue Guard among them); none failed.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The one-holder arm of `packagelessRowHeldBaseAddress`: right.** The new equality (the base is among the candidates exactly when there are two or more) answers the base with two or more holders only when the base is one of them (the #34681 arm, unchanged), and with one holder only when that holder is not the base. `rowHeldBaseAddressOf` is asked, not copied, so every exclusion of the read's judgment stands: a type with no members, a shipped name, an environment item at the member, a disabled row holder, a declined row, a customization pair among the holders, zero or two bases.
- **The canonical member (#33210 contract review S1): not moved, right.** With only the dependent holding the member, `atMember.has(base)` is false and `rowHeldBaseAddressOf` returns the base only when `overlayMemberValue(...)` is a string, which it is not for the canonical member, named or not. The helper returns `undefined`, the publish-mode save keeps `address.packageId`, and the draft wrapper returns `pending`. Pinned in the test's `c_s1` control (bare read 200 at the dependent, bare save receipt `package=` the dependent, rows asserted).
- **The other callers of the widened helper: no cell moves through them.** Each was read for a state where the helper now answers a base it did not answer on `main` (one bound holder, no package-less row at the member):
  - delete, active (`protocol-diff-delete-load.ts`, the guard on two or more `rowsAtAddress.candidates`): asked with two or more candidates only. Not moved.
  - draft discard and per-item publish, `kind === 'ambiguous'`: the draft address is ambiguous either with two or more active candidates (the unchanged arm) or with no active row bound to a package (`active.packageId === null` needs zero candidates, since `packagelessAddress` names the one candidate even beside a package-less row); with zero candidates the helper returns `undefined` on its new first line. The cell the dispatch asked about (drafts of two packages over an active row held by the dependent alone) is not `ambiguous` on `main` either: it is `none` or `draft` keyed on the dependent, and it moves through the new wrapper, which the changeset declares.
  - history, diff, rollback (`historySlotOf`, guarded on two or more slots): two slots with one bound holder means the second slot is the package-less row; the helper returns `undefined` on `address.unbound`. Not moved.
  - publish-mode save, the arm for two or more `address.candidates`: unchanged.
  So the changeset's "Not moved" list (delete, history, diff, rollback at this member) agrees with the tree. The invariant is the callers' guards plus the helper's `unbound` return, not the helper's own; see N3.
- **The publish-mode save's one-holder branch: right.** Asked after `packagelessHolderRefusal`, and only when `servedPackagelessSaveAddress` declined, so every earlier refusal stands; the resolved package is set on `request`, so the inherited named-base rule, the late override re-judgment and the writable-package gate judge the base.
- **The draft-mode follow (`draftAddress.kind === 'ambiguous' || draftAddress.into !== null`): right.** The widened condition asks the helper for every address bound to a package; it answers a base only at the moved cell. Setting `draftAddress = undefined` skips the draft-mode `packagelessHolderRefusal`; at the cell that refusal cannot fire (the judgment already excludes a disabled row holder and a second unrelated base, and the two enabled packages keep `every.some(enabled)` true), so no refusal is lost.
- **`packagelessRowHeldBaseDraftAddress`'s return shape: matches every consumer, with one sub-cell wrong (S1).** `strictDraftReadAddress` reads `kind` and `key`; the publish reads `kind`, `key`, `into`, `drafts.candidates`; the discard reads `kind`, `key`, `into`, `drafts`; the save reads `kind`, `key`, `into`, `drafts`. All four fields are present and typed as the union. `drafts` left as every stored draft binding is what the receipts want: the publish's `others` and the discard's remaining-rows phrase then name the dependent's draft. The sub-cell where the stored draft is package-unbound is S1.
- **Read-only base: right.** With a code package as the row-held base, the bare save resolves the base and the D1 gate (`intent === 'runtime-only' && !host.isWritablePackage(request.packageId)`) refuses `WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED` / 422 naming it, the path the named request takes. Pinned (`ro_cell`: code and status asserted, equal to the named request's, rows unchanged).

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/metadata-protocol: patch` with `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, a **BREAKING** banner and the ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: the right declaration. No key, accepted value or meaning of authored metadata moves, so the level axis gives `patch` (AGENTS.md: "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition"); `major` is barred in the launch window; the narrowing arm is right because a published accept set narrows (the bare per-item publish of the dependent's lone draft: 200 to `404 NO_DRAFT`) and the row a bare write lands in moves, the epic ruling's own "D's row silently updated → E's row (narrowing)" line. The disposition is right: no stored row is rewritten and no author-writable name is removed. `Check Changeset` is `success` on the head.

The FROM/TO list names the REST `PUT`, the in-process save (both modes), the draft read, the per-item publish and the draft discard, which is every door the diff moves. Two gaps between the text and the tree:
- the package-unbound draft at the cell is moved and not listed (S1);
- the banner says the base "holds the item's canonical member"; the code moves the cell whenever the base holds a row of ANY other member (a base holding only `de-DE` beside a dependent's `fr-FR` is the same cell, by `rowHeldBaseJudgment`). Folded into S1's changeset edit; alone it would be a nit.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev reports 7148652912 and 7159591353: `open_questions` empty in both. The declared deviation (the file surface widened to `protocol.ts`, moving the bare draft read, publish and discard with the draft save) is accepted: a bare draft save that wrote a draft no bare draft door reached would have been a new read/write split, and the facade's `packagelessDraftAddress` is the one resolution those doors share. The two out-of-scope findings (the bare delete, history, diff and rollback at the cell; a code-shipped base) are not built here and are left to the seat's filing.
- The card left the direction open ("the read follows the dependent, or the write refuses"). The diff takes the epic ruling 6781691009 literally, "a write resolves its address exactly as the read at the same address resolves it": the read is unchanged and the write follows it. No ruling is re-made here.
- SQL push-down: no new id materialisation and no in-app join. The helper adds one `readItemActiveRows` read, taken only for a bundled type the registry reads by package; a bare draft save at such a type now takes that read twice (once in the wrapper, once in the follow). Not a finding.
- Security: no hunk changes who may write. A bare write that resolves to the base is judged by the same gates as the request naming it: the inherited named-base rule (`uninstalledNamedBaseRefusal`, `followedBase` in draft mode), the late override verdict, and the writable-package gate. The gates asked before the address is resolved (`packagelessOverlayWriteRefusal`, `namedBaseOverlayWriteRefusal`, the flow-scoped `tenantAuthoredWriteRefusal`) concern a name a package ships or a `flow`, neither of which reaches this arm.

### ④ Design judgment

**S1 (should-fix) — the package-unbound draft at the cell is moved, undeclared, unpinned, and the bare discard's receipt denies a stored draft.** `packagelessRowHeldBaseDraftAddress` rewrites every address with `into !== null`, which includes `{ kind: 'draft', key: null, into: DEPENDENT }`: a package-unbound draft at the member over the dependent's lone active row (reachable: a bare draft save at `fr-FR` while no package held that member is the package-unbound draft by `unboundItemDraftAddress`; the dependent's row stored afterwards gives this state). The wrapper answers `{ kind: 'none', key: BASE, into: BASE }`, deciding `kind` from `drafts.candidates` alone and never reading `key === null` or `drafts.unbound`.
  - FROM (`main`): the bare draft read served that draft, the bare publish promoted it into the dependent (200), the bare discard removed it, the bare draft save adopted it.
  - TO (this head): the bare publish finds no draft at the base's key (`404`); the bare draft save writes a second draft bound to the base beside it; the bare discard reaches the last arm of the delete door and answers `No pending draft for TYPE/NAME.` while that draft is stored. The same discard naming the base answers "...so nothing was discarded:" followed by the remaining package-unbound draft (the `request.packageId != null` arm), and so does the #34681 two-holder arm, which sets `request.packageId`. So here the bare request does NOT answer as the request naming the base does, against the changeset's own sentence, and the receipt states something false about the store.
  - Neither the changeset's FROM/TO nor the test names this sub-cell.
  Fix, either way: (a) keep the stored address where the draft it names is the package-unbound one (`address.key === null`), and say so in the wrapper's docblock and the changeset's "Not moved"; or (b) keep the move, make the bare discard's receipt name the remaining package-unbound draft as the named request's does, and add the sub-cell to the FROM/TO. Pin whichever is chosen (bare draft read, publish and discard over a package-unbound draft at the cell, against `?package=BASE`). With the same edit, widen the banner's "holds the item's canonical member" to the base holding a row of another member.

No must-fix.

Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract; none needs a fix on this head):
- N1. At the cell, two sentences outside the diff are now reached with a premise that is loose at the member grain: `packagelessPublishNoDraftRefusal` and the discard's `kind === 'none'` receipt both call the base "the package its published rows are bound to", while the published row at that member is the dependent's. Code and status are right and the remedy they give (name the package) is right. Follow-up card or accepted deviation.
- N2. Published text left stale, deferred by the PR to #35529: `SaveMetaItemRequestSchema.packageId` ("An `active` save then writes the row of the one package the item's active rows are bound to", and the matching draft sentence), the publish and delete `packageId` descriptions, and `rowHeldBaseAddressOf`'s docblock ("where their rows' address names two or more packages"). #35529's items N4 to N6 as filed cover the two-holder exception only and do not name this one-holder cell, so the deferral lands nowhere until that card is amended. The seat adds the cell to #35529 (or files its own card); graded as the #35450 review graded the same class (its N4).
- N3. The helper's docblock says the bare delete, history, diff and rollback "ask only with two or more holders". True today, but it is each caller's guard that makes it so (and for `historySlotOf`, whose guard counts the package-less slot, the helper's `unbound` return). No pin holds those four doors at the cell: the "Not moved" line for them rests on the dev's measurement and on this reading. A control per door in the follow-up would hold it.
- N4. Test 4 asserts that the bare publish and discard equal the named ones (`seen.bare` equals `seen.named`) and the rows, not the literal `NO_DRAFT` / 404 the changeset declares. The equality is the contract the PR states, so the pin is sound; the literal would read better beside it.

Controls, as asked: the canonical member both hold (`c_shared`: receipt package and rows), the canonical member only the dependent holds (`c_s1`: read 200 at the dependent, receipt, rows), unrelated holders at a shared member (`c_unrel`: read and save `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` / 409 naming both) and at a member one holds (`c_unrel_fr`), and a code-shipped base (`shipmail`: read 404, receipt package, rows) each carry a code, status or row assertion. The controls exercise the publish-mode save and the read; the draft doors at those cells are held by the code reading in ① only.

<details><summary>Brief</summary>

## Contract review brief — PR #37069 @ `db0a77a90995c5c6487a521978f1cd05d86b3062` (card #35524)

You review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Render ONE `## Contract review` record on this head — its shape is
`node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --template` — with a PASS or FAIL verdict, and post it as ONE comment
on the PR or its card.

Inputs — these and nothing else:
  · card #35524: its body and EVERY comment (rulings and earlier records included)
  · PR #37069: its body, its file list, and the net diff against `main` at `db0a77a90995c5c6487a521978f1cd05d86b3062`
  · the check-runs on `db0a77a90995c5c6487a521978f1cd05d86b3062`: their conclusions ARE the gate verdicts
⛔ Not the dispatch order, ⛔ not the dispatching seat's own conclusions — this brief is adversarial by design.

Scope — the paths `reviewFace` returns as `hits` on this PR's file list: (narrowing face: the whole diff outside the prose faces) packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-bare-save-dependent-only-member-35524.test.ts;
  plus every file IN THIS DIFF that directly implements or enforces them — the gate that enforces a rule, the code
  a jsdoc or schema line describes, the validator a skill teaches — reviewed for agreement with the contract.
  Widen it freely, ⛔ never below `hits`; the record's `Scope:` line names the implementing files apart from `hits`.
  The rest of the diff (tests, unrelated modules, lockfiles, generated output, changesets) is the lane seat's
  ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, exactly as a standalone PR of those files.
  ④ judges the `hits` files and those implementing files ONLY:
  lockfiles, generated output, changesets and prose elsewhere in the PR are not reviewed;
  code outside the diff is READ to judge them, never reviewed.

Security — if a `hits` path is under `skills/**` or `ui/skills/**` and the change teaches security, auth or permission
  behaviour the path name doesn't show, the record says so and the seat adopting the record adds the `security` label.
  The record says so on its `Security-touching:` line, and the arm lands on `no` alone: write `no` ONLY when no changed
  hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential, token, authentication or other security behaviour, else `yes`.

Rule change — if a `hits` path is under `.claude/**`: the PR body declares `Rule-change:` and you verify it against the diff.
  Write `Rule-change-verified: none` ONLY when no changed hunk alters what an agent may do without the maintainer
  (merge, bypass a check, change repository settings), what gets done and in what order (grading, dispatch, scope), or
  what must go to him (decisions, maintainer actions); process steps, scripts, wording, slimming and file moves are not rule
  changes. Write `ruled` ONLY when every such hunk copies the ruling the PR body quotes on its `Ruling-ref:` line — check the
  copy against the quoted words, do not re-rule it. Otherwise `yes`: the pull request then waits for the maintainer.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
